question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund is an open-ended Category III AIF with investable funds of INR 400 crore. The fund manager wants to build a position in Company Alpha (listed). What is the MAXIMUM amount the fund can invest in Company Alpha, based on investable funds (i.e., not NAV)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Category III AIFs may invest up to 10% of investable funds in a single investee company (directly or through units of other AIFs). 10% × INR 400 cr = INR 40 crore. For listed equity, the same 10% may be calculated alternatively on NAV. LVFs of Category III get 20%; the general Cat III cap is 10%. The Trap: Option B (25%) is the Cat I/II close-ended concentration limit — swapped category. Option C (20%) is the LVF-for-AI concession — fund is not LVF. Option D (15%) is a distractor. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D tests 25% Cat I/II concentration. XIX-C tests both. XIX-E fixes on 10% Cat III (20% only for LVFs). Manager's Pro-Tip: For listed-equity pair trades, you can measure the cap against NAV — useful when MTM pushes NAV above investable funds. For unlisted/derivative exposures, only investable funds can be the denominator.
